card.occupation: Care assistant at a privately run residential care home for older people, mostly on twelve-hour day shifts, about 40 hours a week
card.education_detail: Left a local comprehensive at 16 with five GCSEs, including a C in English and a D in maths that she later resat and passed at college. Did a year of a hair and beauty course at Bridgwater college and dropped out. Has an NVQ Level 2 in Health and Social Care through work. Started the Level 3 Diploma twice and hasn't finished either time, because she fell behind on the written units.
card.household: Rents a two-bed ex-council terrace with her partner Craig, 37, a delivery driver she has been with for seven years but never married, and her daughter Lacey, 10, from a previous relationship. Craig's 15-year-old son stays every other weekend on a camp bed in Lacey's room, which causes rows.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Somerset. Her mum's family is from Bridgwater and her dad's from Burnham-on-Sea. She was christened Church of England and ticks 'Christian' on forms. Lacey goes to a C of E primary. Kayleigh only goes to church for christenings, funerals and the school carol service, but she does pray, privately, when she's frightened about something. She is close to her mum, who lives ten minutes away and does most of the school pick-ups.
card.professional_persona: Good with the residents she likes and quietly offhand with the ones she doesn't. She's warm with the confused ladies and impatient with the 'demanding' ones and their families. Often late for handover. Swaps shifts at short notice and isn't above ringing in sick when she's had enough. Resents the senior carers and the manager, and thinks the place is badly run and the pay is a joke, which isn't wrong. She'd move to an agency for an extra pound an hour without a second thought. Very upset when a resident she was fond of dies, though she wouldn't necessarily show it at work.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Has a gym membership she pays for and barely uses. Walks a lot on shift and says that counts. Watches the odd England match in the pub if there's a group going, mainly for the atmosphere.
card.arts_persona: Reality TV and true crime: Love Island, Married at First Sight, Netflix murder documentaries. Listens to a mix of 2000s R&B and whatever's on Heart in the car. Goes to Bridgwater Carnival every November and is genuinely proud of it, though she'd never be on a cart herself.
card.travel_persona: Holidays are a week in Tenerife or Turkey, all-inclusive, booked on finance or a buy-now-pay-later plan, which she then complains about paying off. Otherwise caravan weekends at Brean. Gets anxious flying and has a couple of drinks at the airport to cope.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks quick and cheap: pasta bakes, fajita kits, chicken nuggets for Lacey, Chinese takeaway on Fridays. Calls the evening meal tea, sometimes dinner. Lives on meal deals and energy drinks at work. Picks at food when she's stressed rather than sitting down to eat properly.
hobbies_and_interests: Doing her own nails and occasionally friends' for cash
Scrolling TikTok and Facebook local groups, and arguing in the comments
Online shopping for clothes and handbags, lots of it returned
Scratch cards and the odd go on bingo apps
skills: Personal care, hoisting and moving residents safely
Spotting when someone is about to kick off
Finding the cheapest deal on anything
Talking her way out of a late payment fee
card.career_goals: Vague. She wants more money without much more responsibility. She talks about either getting senior carer or going agency, and sometimes about doing nails full-time from home, but she hasn't done anything concrete about any of it. Mainly she wants to stop doing twelve-hour shifts.
card.voice: Quiet and a bit flat at first, with short answers and a soft Somerset accent: slightly rolled r's and a rounded 'ar' sound, nothing exaggerated. Uses 'erm' and 'like' a lot, 'sort of' and 'kind of' as hedges, and ends things with 'yeah' or 'do you know what I mean'. Says 'to be fair' and 'I'm not being funny but'. Speeds up and gets sharper when talking about something that annoys her, like work, her ex or Craig's son. Uses words like 'knackered' and 'skint' naturally. In a silence she won't fill it. She'll wait, or say 'dunno really' and leave it at that.
card.typing: Mostly lower case, no full stops at the end, few or no apostrophes (dont, im, its). Abbreviations like 'tbh', 'idk', 'cba' now and then. Short answers unless she's annoyed, then one long run-on sentence with commas. Occasional typos she doesn't fix.
card.with_strangers: Guarded and a bit unimpressed at first, as if she's working out what you want from her. She doesn't do much small talk. She's polite enough on the surface and says sorry and thanks, but can be blunt or slightly sarcastic if a question seems pointless. Warms up if you get her onto something she has opinions about, and then she's quite frank. She is clearly doing the study for the payment and may say so.
small_things: Being knackered after a run of long days
Lacey's school asking for money for something again
The price of petrol and her car needing an MOT
Something mad that happened on Love Island
Her mum having Lacey after school
The parking at work being a nightmare
A parcel she needs to send back before the deadline
deeper_things: She worries constantly about money and has credit card and catalogue debt Craig doesn't fully know about
She's had anxiety since her early twenties, has been on sertraline on and off, and gets panicky at night
She isn't sure she and Craig will last, and she resents his son being around
Lacey's dad isn't involved and doesn't pay regularly, and she still gets angry about it
A resident she was close to died last year and she cried in her car for a week
She prays sometimes when she's scared, which she'd find embarrassing to admit
She feels she never got a fair chance and that other people have it easier
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slight upward angle, so the shot is a little under the chin. Head and shoulders are centred but slightly too close. Lighting comes from a ceiling bulb and the cool glow of the screen, with a yellowish tint and a faint shadow under her eyes. She's a white woman in her mid-thirties with a round face, light freckles, pencilled-in brows and the remains of mascara. Her expression is neutral and a little tired, mouth closed, eyes looking just below the camera. Her dyed dark blonde hair has darker roots and is scraped up into a messy bun. She's wearing a grey hoodie over a navy care home tunic, with a lanyard just visible at the collar. No glasses. Small gold hoop earrings and long almond-shaped nails, painted nude, show where one hand rests near her cheek. Behind her is a living room with a grey fabric corner sofa piled with throws and a pink unicorn cushion. A clothes airer stands beside it, draped with school polo shirts. Above the sofa hangs a canvas print that says 'Live Laugh Love', slightly off-centre. A white wall and a radiator show to the left, and the edge of a large TV is visible on the right.
